biography.concept: Drum-keeper — Shaman association, echo of Toblerone
biography.notes: Kept the rhythm steady the night Toblerone's spirit-walk ran long and nearly didn't come back, and still won't say what she saw in the gap between beats.

description.value:
"The dead are fine. It's the living who need tending."

Keeper is the Soul Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: priest, ritualist, medium, hedge-warden, funeral speaker. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Hearthlight: Allies within near range add +1 Resolve (+2 at Tier III). The congregation stands straighter when the Keeper is present.

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Faith rank = tier; secondary Insight rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Soft Power marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Pactkeeper or Dreamwalker. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Keeper — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — The rites: Weddings, funerals, blessings; participants recover 2×tier Stress between scenes. Standard fee 10 marks (Soft Power).

Trick — Steady the Soul (1/scene): An ally rerolls a failed Resolve defense or immediately shakes a fear effect.

Echoes are the past made flesh — people out of a Steward's former lives, walking beside them again. Ren Achak is an echo of Toblerone's time with the Shaman occult association. Being remembered leaves a mark.

Drum-keeper — Kept the rhythm steady the night Toblerone's spirit-walk ran long and nearly didn't come back, and still won't say what she saw in the gap between beats.

Spirit Ledger — Apprentice (Echo Boon)

Once per scene, ask the spirits of the place one yes/no question; they answer truthfully (GM voice).

Echo's Mark: while their Steward can see them, the echo adds +1 on any check made in direct support of the Steward.

The local spirits keep accounts, and this one is owed.

Human. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Cro-Magnon, Denisovan, Florensis, Neanderthal.

This root grants the shared Human core trait package and preserves live UUID compatibility for existing feature items.

“Humanity is not special. It’s just stubborn enough to keep moving when reality begs it to stop.”

Adaptive. 1/Soma Break, when you fail a check, you can choose to succeed instead.

Tenacious. While you have 1 Integrity, you reroll the lowest die on one check of your choice each round (declare before rolling).

Lineage Memory. Choose one human lineage (Cro-Magnon, Denisovan, Florensis, Neanderthal). Your lineage grants Tier powers as you level.

New Heritage (v2). Cro-Magnon replaces Erectus in the Human heritage lineup.

“Humanity is the species that keeps walking even when the map says ‘stop.’”

Human (Cro-Magnon). You are not a fantasy human. You are the cognitive, symbolic, cooperative inheritance of the lineage that first painted ancestors on cave walls, buried its dead with flowers, and traded ochre across a continent it had no map for.

Where Neanderthal is strength and Florensis is reach, Cro-Magnon is pattern. Language, ritual, coalition. You are the human branch that kept explaining things until the explanation started working.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid.

  • Size. Medium.

  • Speed. 6 squares

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward MND (Mind) or PRE (Presence)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Stubborn Spark

At creation you gain Stubborn Spark (Adaptive, Tenacious, Lineage Memory).

Cro-Magnon Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Cro-Magnon powers emphasize: Symbolic Thought (ritual and language sensitivity), Coalition Instinct (cooperation bonuses with allies), Tool Mind (improvisational tool use), and Narrative Memory (lore retention that persists across generations).

Leather-wrapped lead-shot bludgeon, palm-sized. Lives in a pocket or a sleeve. Designed to put someone out without breaking anything that won't heal in a week.

Standard Issue (Subdual). Damage is subdual-flavored — narratively kinetic but easy to declare nonlethal. Useful for Couriers, intriguers, and anyone whose plan ended with "and then we walk away."

  • Faculty: Violence
  • Attack: Melee (Violence)
  • Reach: Melee
  • Duration: Scene
  • Tier: T1

description.value:
Undyed sept-cloth cut to a long working robe with a corded belt. Issued to first-circle initiates of any chapterhouse or tutor-cell — the kind of garment that gets traded between students faster than any of them keep notebooks. Comfortable to channel in. Forgettable to anyone watching for trouble.

Standard Issue. Light enough to manifest in. Dignified enough to walk past a sept-warden.

⚙️ Mechanical Effects

  • Armor: Cloth
  • Defense: Evasion +1, Resolve +1
  • Requires: Weave (trained)
  • Tier: I
  • Cost: 75 Nonlethal marks
